:::{#rem-elementwise-function-notation}
#### Notation and software for elementwise application

- The superscript $\odot$ keeps $f^{\odot}$ apart from $f$ itself.
  Where a function $f$ takes a whole vector as its argument,
  as in the multivariable calculus of [vector calculus](vector-calculus.qmd),
  $f(\vx)$ means $f$ evaluated at the vector,
  which is generally not the vector of its values at the entries.
- If $f$ has parameters, as in $f_{\vb}$,
  the same parameters are used at every entry.
- Software usually applies a scalar function to a vector this way,
  without a special symbol:
  R and NumPy evaluate `exp(x)` entry by entry.
  The matrix exponential of a square matrix is a different function from $\operatorname{exp}^{\odot}$.

:::
